dfm_alerts.description: The flight battery has no specified restraint, electrical protection, venting or clearance from the ESC and other heat sources; a loose or damaged pack is a safety risk.
dfm_alerts.fix: Define a positive-retention battery compartment, protected pack and connector, insulated routing, thermal clearance and a safe vent path; validate against the applicable battery safety requirements.

dfm_alerts.description: The shell specification combines an injection-moulded PA12-GF body with carbon-fibre arms, while the BOM lists folding arms separately. The arm-to-shell joint and assembly sequence are undefined.
dfm_alerts.fix: Specify the arms as separate parts and define hinge inserts, retention, load path, assembly access and inspection criteria.
dfm_alerts.rule_citation: Define inserts and assembly interfaces before tooling — Protolabs injection molding design guide

dfm_alerts.description: The self-tapping screw type is unspecified, so the stated boss pilot cannot be verified for installation torque, stripping or repeated battery-service cycles.
dfm_alerts.fix: Select a specific screw for plastics; validate pilot diameter, engagement, boss outside diameter and installation torque in moulded samples. Use inserts where repeated removal is required.
dfm_alerts.rule_citation: Size screw bosses and pilot holes to the selected fastener — Protolabs injection molding design guide

dfm_alerts.description: Shell mating-face tolerances and the split-line step limit lack datum references and an assembled stack-up. Independent part inspection cannot establish whether assembled shells will meet the step limit.
dfm_alerts.fix: Define locating datums and alignment features, then tolerance the assembled interface using a stack-up and inspection fixture.
dfm_alerts.rule_citation: Establish datums and control features in relation to assembly function — ISO 1101

dfm_alerts.description: The PA12-GF enclosure has no flame-rating requirement despite housing a LiPo battery and power electronics. Its UV and saltwater resistance are also unspecified for kitesurf use.
dfm_alerts.fix: Specify a qualified enclosure grade and required flame rating; validate UV, salt-spray and moisture exposure on finished assemblies.
dfm_alerts.rule_citation: Plastic-material flammability classification — UL 94; salt-spray testing — ISO 9227

dfm_alerts.description: No sealing scheme is specified for the shell split, camera, card access, wiring exits or fasteners. Spray and saltwater ingress could damage the electronics.
dfm_alerts.fix: Set an ingress-protection target and define gaskets, connector seals, drain strategy and production leak-test criteria.
dfm_alerts.rule_citation: Degrees of protection provided by enclosures — IEC 60529

dfm_alerts.description: Minimum wall draft is 1.46°: enough for a polished finish, short of the ~3° a textured finish ('Matte · Graphite #3A3D42') needs.
dfm_alerts.fix: Increase draft to 3° on textured faces, or specify a lighter texture / polished finish.
dfm_alerts.rule_citation: Draft ≥1° plus 1° per 0.025 mm texture depth — Protolabs injection molding design guidelines; measured with text-to-cad DFM skill (mold_tool.py, MIT) ported to OCCT

measurement.label: measured
measurement.source_or_assumption: Min wall draft vs pull +Z: lowest-draft B-rep wall face ≥ 48.52 mm² (curved, 228.92 mm² at [-46.26, 22.26, 9.76]) — text-to-cad DFM skill (mold_tool.py, MIT) ported to OCCT

dfm_alerts.description: Projected area along +Z: 6602 mm² (part silhouette, per cavity). Estimated clamp force ≈ 33.8 t (Estimate: area in² × 3.0 t/in² for PC/ABS × 1.1 safety) — per cavity; a family tool moulding both shells in one shot roughly doubles it.
dfm_alerts.fix: Quote on a press ≥ 50 t; keep both shells in one family mould only if tonnage allows.
dfm_alerts.rule_citation: Clamp force ≈ projected area × cavity-pressure factor (2-5 t/in²) — Protolabs injection molding design guidelines; silhouette raster from text-to-cad DFM skill (mold_tool.py, MIT) ported to OCCT

measurement.label: measured

dfm_alerts.description: Measured wall 2.00-2.00 mm is within the PC/ABS 1.2-3.5 mm range; keep bosses/ribs ≤ 60% of nominal wall to avoid sink.
dfm_alerts.fix: No change to nominal wall; core bosses and ribs to ≤ 60% of the wall.
dfm_alerts.rule_citation: PC/ABS wall 1.2-3.5 mm, ribs/bosses ≤ 60% of wall — Protolabs injection molding design guidelines

questions.en: DFM critical — The flight battery has no specified restraint, electrical protection, venting or clearance from the ESC and other heat sources; a loose or damaged pack is a safety risk. Proposed fix: Define a positive-retention battery compartment, protected pack and connector, insulated routing, thermal clearance and a safe vent path; validate against the applicable battery safety requirements. Can you accommodate this, and at what cost or lead-time impact?
questions.cn: DFM 关键问题 — 飞行电池未规定固定方式、电气保护、排气通道以及与电调(ESC)及其他热源的间距;电池包松动或损坏属于安全风险。建议方案:定义具有可靠固定的电池仓、受保护的电池包及连接器、绝缘走线、热间距和安全排气路径;并依据适用的电池安全要求进行验证。贵司能否满足此要求?对成本和交期有何影响?

standards.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/945 on unmanned aircraft systems (class marks C0-C6)
standards.applies_because: EU market: the drone must carry a class mark (C0 < 250 g, C1 < 900 g, C2 < 4 kg MTOM) with the class requirements (speed, geo-awareness, remote ID)

standards.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/947 on the rules and procedures for the operation of unmanned aircraft
standards.applies_because: EU operating rules the class mark unlocks (open category A1/A2/A3) — what the buyer may do with it

standards.title: Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (FAA)
standards.applies_because: US small UAS operating rules (commercial use, < 55 lb)

standards.title: Registration and Marking Requirements for Small Unmanned Aircraft (FAA)
standards.applies_because: US registration of small unmanned aircraft above the weight threshold

standards.title: Remote Identification of Unmanned Aircraft (FAA)
standards.applies_because: US Remote ID broadcast requirement for registered drones

standards.title: FCC Part 15 — Radio Frequency Devices
standards.applies_because: 2.4 / 5.8 GHz control and video link (FCC 15C) + digital device (15B)

standards.title: Radio Equipment Directive (RED)
standards.applies_because: Radio link sold in the EU (RED)

standards.title: Secondary cells and batteries containing alkaline or other non-acid electrolytes — Safety — Part 2: Lithium systems
UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, section 38.3 (lithium batteries)
standards.applies_because: Lithium battery shipped with the product

risks.risk: All-up weight creeps over the class limit (C0 250 g / C1 900 g) with the battery and gimbal
risks.mitigation: Weight budget per part from day one; weigh every prototype; two battery options per class

risks.risk: Flight-controller / ESC failure → fly-away or crash over people
risks.mitigation: Certified flight-controller module with geofence, return-to-home and low-battery landing; ESC current telemetry

risks.risk: Salt spray and sand at the beach (kitesurf use) corrode motors and gimbal
risks.mitigation: Sealed bearings, conformal-coated PCBA, IP43 target on the body, rinse guidance

risks.risk: Wind: gusts above 10 m/s exceed the hover margin of a light drone
risks.mitigation: Thrust-to-weight ≥ 2, wind-speed warning in the app, EASA C-class wind rating on the label

risks.risk: Video link drops over water at distance
risks.mitigation: Dual-band link with diversity antennas; follow-me distance cap

tests.name: Hover endurance and thrust stand
tests.method: Thrust stand per motor/prop, then hover to 20% battery at sea level

tests.name: Drop / crash test of arms and gimbal
tests.method: Drop from 1.5 m on each arm; hinge and gimbal functional check

tests.name: Salt mist on motors and fasteners
tests.method: 48 h 5% NaCl fog, bearing and contact inspection

checks.name: Hover flight time from battery energy and hover power
checks.threshold: ≥ 25 min pass, ≥ 15 min warn (category target, Estimate)

build_strategy.title: Module assembly
build_strategy.explanation: You design the product around bought-in, pre-certified modules (e.g. motor + driver, battery pack, radio module, heater + fan): your work is the architecture, the enclosure, the integration and the software; the factory assembles the modules into your parts. Faster and cheaper than designing every sub-system, and the modules' certifications carry part of the compliance.
